extracted.intended_audience: NLP / computational-linguistics researchers and HCI researchers studying automated creativity evaluation and creative-writing assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the creativity of short stories using the proposed Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW), a set of 14 binary tests organized into classic creativity dimensions, assessed via expert human judges (Consensual Assessment Technique).

rubrics_metrics.name: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW) — 14 binary tests
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW consists of 14 binary tests organized into the original dimensions of Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to evaluate creativity as a product; each test is binary (pass/fail). The paper uses TTCW to assess 48 stories written by professionals or LLMs via human judges. (Original phrasing from abstract: 'TTCW consists of 14 binary tests organized into the original dimensions of Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency (TTCW dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions: Fluency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an organizing dimension for the TTCW binary tests. The abstract does not list the specific Fluency tests; Fluency typically captures the number of ideas/responses produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility (TTCW dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions: Flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an organizing dimension for the TTCW binary tests. The abstract does not enumerate the exact Flexibility tests; Flexibility ordinarily measures variety across categories or shifts in perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (TTCW dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions: Originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an organizing dimension for the TTCW binary tests. The abstract does not provide item-level definitions; Originality generally assesses novelty or uncommonness of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaboration (TTCW dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the original TTCW dimensions: Elaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as an organizing dimension for the TTCW binary tests. The abstract does not give specific Elaboration items; Elaboration commonly measures detail, development, and expansion of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the Consensual Assessment Technique (CAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study uses the Consensual Assessment Technique to implement human assessment of stories when applying TTCW.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAT implies using expert human judges (here, 10 creative writers) to rate creative products. In this work CAT is combined with TTCW to produce binary pass/fail judgments on each test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate creativity as a product (not process)
rubrics_metrics.description: TTCW is proposed to evaluate creativity as a product, inspired by the Torrance Test of Creative Thinking (TTCT), which measures creativity as a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction matters methodologically: TTCW operationalizes product-level, observable outputs (stories) via binary tests, rather than process-oriented measures. The abstract emphasizes this orientation but does not provide further operational details on process vs product criteria.
